title: Dual-isotope narrow-line MOT of dysprosium by phase modulation
authors: M. Dürbeck, L. Reihs, J. Seifert, B. Choudhari, J. P. Marulanda-Serna, N. Werum, M. De Pas, G. Meijer, G. Valtolina
abstract: We report on the characterization of a narrow-line magneto-optical trap (MOT), where two different isotopes of the dysprosium (Dy) atom can be simultaneously loaded and trapped. We rely on phase modulation via high-power, free-space electro-optic modulators (EOMs) to generate optical sidebands at the correct detuning for two different isotopes. This technique is applied on the slowing transition at 421 nm and the MOT transition at 626 nm. Using modular resonant electronic circuits, we match the sideband separation to the isotope shift among the two target isotopes, realizing mixtures of the bosonic isotopes 164Dy -162Dy and 162Dy -160Dy. We exploit the interplay between radiation forces and gravity in the narrow-line MOT to control the spatial position of the two isotopes with the EOM drive frequency. We demonstrate full control of the isotopic mixture with the EOM drive, offering new and cost-effective capabilities for controlling mixtures of atomic species that can be trapped in a narrow-line MOT.
summary: The research reports on a novel dual-isotope MOT technique for dysprosium using phase modulation via Electro-Optic Modulators. By precisely tuning the EOM drive frequency, the authors achieve simultaneous and controllable trapping of different isotopes in a narrow-line regime. This method provides a highly efficient and versatile tool for studying mixtures of atomic species.
main_problem: The primary goal is characterizing a narrow-line Magneto-Optical Trap (MOT) capable of simultaneously loading and trapping two different isotopes of dysprosium using phase modulation.
main_result: The authors demonstrated full control over the isotopic mixture in the MOT by tuning the Electro-Optic Modulator (EOM) drive frequency, offering a cost-effective method for controlling mixtures of atomic species.
method: They utilized high-power, free-space EOMs to generate optical sidebands at detunings specific to two different isotopes, enabling simultaneous trapping on narrow transitions.
model_or_system: The experiment uses Dysprosium (Dy) atoms, specifically targeting bosonic isotope mixtures like ${}^{164}	ext{Dy} - {}^{162}	ext{Dy}$ and ${}^{162}	ext{Dy} - {}^{160}	ext{Dy}$. Trapping occurs on narrow-line transitions at 626 nm, preceded by cooling at 421 nm.
key_observables: Trapped atom number ($N$), center-of-mass (CoM) shift, and the relative population imbalance between isotopes.
important_parameters: Isotope shift ($\Delta I_S \approx 962 	ext{ MHz}$), EOM drive frequency ($\Omega = \Delta I_S / 2$), and modulation depth ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The technique relies on using non-resonant EOMs with external electronics to overcome bandwidth limitations inherent in built-in LC circuits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electronic structure, the setup geometry, and show how the EOM drive frequency controls the isotopic mixture and causes measurable spatial displacements of the two isotope clouds along the gravity axis.
paper_structure: The paper details the development of a dual-isotope MOT using sidebands from EOMs. It characterizes performance by measuring atom numbers vs. modulation depth, demonstrating control over the relative population imbalance, and mapping CoM shifts to measure $\Delta I_S$.
why_interesting: This work showcases advanced optical techniques (EOM phase modulation) applied to cold atoms for precise isotopic control, which is crucial for quantum simulation platforms requiring multiple atomic species.
